links.outcome: Symptom triage agreement, red-flag recognition, escalation sensitivity, under-triage
links.effect: Triage agreement 75.9%, red-flag recognition 71.1%, escalation sensitivity 77.1%; under-triage and unsafe reassurance remained observable, particularly in high-risk irAE scenarios.
links.quote: In symptom triage, agreement with expert triage levels was 75.9%, red-flag recognition was 71.1%, and escalation sensitivity was 77.1%; under-triage and unsafe reassurance remained observable, particularly in high-risk irAE scenarios.

links.outcome: Proportion of LLM outputs needing revision after nurse review
links.effect: Only 3.7% of outputs required no revision, whereas 31.4% required major revision or withholding.
links.quote: Across all tasks, only 3.7% of outputs required no revision, whereas 31.4% required major revision or withholding.

unlisted_practices: Providing pathology-derived risk context to the LLM to improve triage accuracy (agreement improved from 52.5% to 70.0%)
Local on-premises deployment of a small open-weight LLM for nursing communication support

screen.reason: The study directly evaluates human-in-the-loop specialist nurse review, expert adjudication, and the impact of incorporating pathology-derived risk context on LLM triage safety and revision burden.

primary.practice: clinician review and pathology context integration
